pi.name: Brian Button, PhD
pi.titles:
Professor · Marsico Lung Institute
Department of Biochemistry & Biophysics · UNC School of Medicine
bio: Brian Button studies the biophysics of mucus and how the airway surface defends itself against inhaled insults. His work has helped reframe airway disease as fundamentally a problem of mucus hydration and gel mechanics — a perspective that now informs therapeutic development across cystic fibrosis, COPD, and severe respiratory infection.

He completed his doctoral work in cellular physiology and joined UNC's Marsico Lung Institute to pursue questions at the interface of cell biology and soft-matter physics. The Button Lab today combines microrheology, ion-transport electrophysiology, advanced live-cell imaging, and primary human airway models to ask — at every scale from molecules to patients — how the lung keeps itself clean.

members.name: Mark Gutay
members.bio: Runs lab operations and is an expert in studying mucus clearance mechanisms. He has co-authored many of our papers on understanding mucus clearance in health and disease, including the lab's most recent J Clin Invest paper on cilia-independent mucus transport.

members.name: Courtney Haskins
members.bio: Leads our research on creating models of Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD) to understand how ciliopathies affect mucus properties and its clearance.

members.name: Matt Pappas
members.bio: Works on understanding the role of novel mucinases in airway bacterial infection in cystic fibrosis.

members.name: Catherine "Cricket" Schoettelkotte
members.bio: Investigates how genetic and environmental changes affect the efficiency of cilia- and cough-mediated mucus clearance in the airways.

members.name: Viktoria Gustafsson
members.bio: Investigating novel therapeutics to clear mucus plugs from the airways of people with lung disease.

members.name: Maeve McCann
members.bio: Works with Matt Pappas to understand the role of secreted mucinases in bacterial infections in persons with Cystic Fibrosis.

members.name: Rishika Kommuri
members.bio: Manages our stock of human airway epithelial cultures and organizes the lab.

members.name: Bella Grace
members.bio: Bella is a 1-year old Golden Retriever. She is currently working on her Ph.D. in treatology and becoming a therapy dog. Her research interests include figuring out ways to get the lab members to give her more belly scratches.
